description: This course introduces students to methods in historical research that look beyond the nation-state in examining the past. Students will research a topic in transnational history that interests them, but as a class we will focus on three types of transnational linkages in history -- flows of humans, ideas and commodities -- to explore different strategies and methods for telling interconnected histories. Through an examination of the historical forces that have made our world interconnected yet also unequal, we will pay attention to local histories of global interconnection and ask if the world itself can be thought of as an interconnected system. Drawing on historical research as well as methods from across the disciplines, students will learn dynamic and connective ways to think about the past.
name: Sem: Transnational & Global History
notes: Full topic title: A Transnational and Global History
Not open to incoming first-year students.
